answer: Make per-identity registration cost superlinear: each additional agent an operator runs costs the square of its count, so the Nth clone owes a fee scaling with N. One honest node pays ~1 unit, but 1,000 sybils owe ~500,500 units total. An attacker dodges this by spreading clones across fresh funding sources to look like independent operators, yet each still posts its own rising bond, so the velvet ease of mass cloning drowns under a tide of quadratic cost. Like thinning an orchard, the curve punishes exactly the density a sybil fleet needs.
